title: Lean code at idle from cracked PCV hose
text: Applies to 2.0L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2012-2020. P0171 (system too lean, bank 1) may set with a rough idle that is worst on a cold engine. The PCV hose can crack on its underside where it joins the intake elbow, admitting unmetered air. With the engine idling, inspect the hose at the elbow and flex it gently while listening for a vacuum hiss. Repair: replace the PCV hose and clamp.
step: With the engine idling, inspect the PCV hose where it joins the intake elbow, flexing it gently while you listen for a vacuum hiss
results: I flexed the PCV hose at the elbow with it idling. No cracks and no hiss.
The PCV hose at the elbow looks fine, and I can't hear any hiss even when I bend it.

title: Lean code at idle from intake manifold gasket shrinkage
text: Applies to 2.0L I4 engines, model years 2021-2023, with the revised composite intake manifold. P0171 may set at idle after a cold soak because the manifold-to-head gasket shrinks at low temperature. Smoke-test the intake with the engine cold, concentrating on the manifold-to-head joint. Repair: replace the intake manifold gasket with the updated part.

title: Lean code at steady cruise from sticking purge valve
text: Applies to all gasoline engines with an EVAP purge valve. P0171 may set only during steady cruise above 50 mph on a fully warm engine; idle quality is normal and the code does not set at idle. With a scan tool, command the EVAP purge valve closed and check for vacuum at the canister side of the valve. Use a hand vacuum gauge at the port. Repair: replace the purge valve.

title: Extended crank on cold mornings from fuel pump check valve
text: Applies to 1.8L I4 and 2.0L I4 engines. A long crank may occur only after the vehicle sits overnight below 40 deg F; restarts with a warm engine are normal. Leave a gauge on the rail test port overnight and compare the morning reading with the reading at shutdown. Record the overnight low temperature with both readings. Repair: replace the fuel pump module.

title: Misfire in wet weather from coil boot tracking
text: Applies to all engines with coil-on-plug ignition. A misfire may occur at idle or light throttle only during rain or after a car wash, and it clears once the engine bay dries. Mist water over the coils with the engine idling and watch for arcing at the coil boots in a dark shop. Wear eye protection and keep water away from the alternator. Repair: install updated coil boots and apply dielectric grease.

title: Misfire at light load from intake valve deposits
text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines, model years 2016-2018. A misfire code may set at light-load cruise because carbon deposits on the intake valves disturb airflow on these direct-injection engines. Inspect the intake valves with a borescope through the intake port. Save the borescope images for comparison. Repair: clean the intake valves with the approved media-blast procedure.

title: High coolant temperature at sustained highway speed
text: Applies to all engines with a molded lower radiator hose. Coolant temperature may rise during sustained highway driving or towing while temperature in stop-and-go traffic stays normal. Inspect the lower radiator hose for collapse at high rpm with the engine warm. Have a helper hold the rpm while you watch the hose. Repair: install the reinforced lower hose.

title: Temperature gauge reads high with normal coolant temperature
text: Applies to compact sedans with the 2.0L I4 engine, model years 2020-2022. The temperature gauge may read high in traffic while actual coolant temperature is normal. Compare the gauge with the coolant temperature reading on a scan tool once the engine is fully warm, and note both values. Repair: update the instrument cluster software.

title: Internal coolant loss at intake manifold gasket
text: Applies to 3.4L V6 engines, model years 2020-2022. Coolant loss with no external leak may come from the intake manifold gasket at a coolant passage. Pressure-test the cooling system and inspect the gasket area with a borescope through the throttle body opening. Look for dried coolant crust along the gasket edges. Note how much coolant the system loses per week. Repair: replace the intake manifold gaskets.

title: No heat from rear heater
text: Applies to minivans with a rear heater. The front heater works normally but the rear vents blow cool because the rear heater control valve sticks closed. Command the rear heat on and feel both rear heater hoses under the vehicle. Let the engine reach full operating temperature first. The valve is usually mounted along the frame rail near the rear axle. Repair: replace the rear heater control valve.

title: Dead battery after parking from audio module staying awake
text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. The battery may go flat after the vehicle is parked for two to three days because the audio module fails to enter sleep mode. After the vehicle has been locked for 60 minutes, measure draw at the negative battery terminal and note whether it drops below 50 mA when the radio fuse is pulled. Repair: reprogram the audio module.

title: Battery drain from infotainment head unit
text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. The infotainment head unit may not enter sleep mode after a software update and drain the battery within a few days. Measure parasitic draw and check whether the head unit stays awake. Allow the modules time to sleep first. A clamp-on meter avoids waking the modules when you connect it. Repair: update the head unit software.

title: LED headlamp flicker from lamp driver software
text: Applies to midsize SUVs with LED headlamps, model years 2020-2022. Headlamps may flicker at idle while charging voltage is normal and no battery warning appears. Check the lamp driver module for stored codes, and inspect the lamp connector for corrosion. Record any codes before clearing them. Repair: update the lamp driver module software.

title: Battery warning after auto start-stop restart
text: Applies to 1.4L turbo I4 engines with auto start-stop, model years 2019-2021. The battery warning lamp may flash briefly when the engine restarts after an auto stop. Review battery sensor data and stored body control codes. Drive through several stop cycles so the event is captured. Check that the battery is the type the start-stop system specifies. Repair: replace the battery monitoring sensor.

title: Slow crank after hot soak from starter heat
text: Applies to all vehicles. The engine may turn over slowly, but does turn over, when restarted after a hot soak. Measure starter current draw with an inductive clamp during cranking with fuel disabled. Let the engine sit hot for about 30 minutes to reproduce the condition. Repair: install a starter heat shield or replace the starter.

title: Intermittent no crank from starter relay in underhood fuse block
text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. The starter may intermittently fail to engage because of a weak starter relay in the underhood fuse block. Swap the starter relay with an identical relay and retest several times, since the fault is intermittent. Repair: replace the starter relay.

title: Low-speed pulsation felt in the seat from rear drums
text: Applies to hatchbacks with rear drum brakes. A pulsation felt through the seat, not the steering wheel, may occur during light stops below 25 mph from out-of-round rear drums. Measure rear drum diameter at several points and compare with the limit cast inside the drum. Repair: replace the rear drums.

title: Brake vibration while towing
text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A brake vibration may occur only during stops while towing a trailer over 5,000 lb. Check trailer brake gain settings and inspect rotors for heat spots. Reproduce the condition with the same trailer and load. Record the trailer weight and the gain setting before any adjustment. Repair: install revised front rotors.

title: Brake pull from caliper bracket casting
text: Applies to midsize SUVs, model years 2022-2024. A pull during braking may occur because of a front caliper bracket casting variation that holds the outer pad off-center. Inspect the bracket part number stamp against the bulletin list on both sides, since either bracket can be affected. Repair: replace both front caliper brackets.

title: Hard brake pedal at idle from booster check valve
text: Applies to 2.0L I4 engines. The brake pedal may feel hard and require high effort at idle because the brake booster check valve sticks. Measure vacuum at the booster with the engine idling, using a gauge teed into the booster hose. It should read at least 18 inHg at a warm idle. Listen for a hiss at the pedal while the engine idles. Repair: replace the booster check valve and hose.

title: Rear clunk over bumps from leaf spring shackles
text: Applies to full-size pickups. A clunk from the rear of the truck over bumps may come from dry leaf spring shackle bushings. Inspect the rear shackles for play with the truck on the ground, using a pry bar between the shackle and the frame bracket. Repair: replace the shackle bushings.

title: Front clunk from loose subframe bolts
text: Applies to compact crossovers, model years 2021-2023. A clunk over bumps may come from front subframe mounting bolts that lost torque. Check subframe bolt torque with the vehicle on the ground, and look for shiny witness marks around the bolt heads. A torque wrench and a helper to watch the subframe over bumps make the check quicker. Repair: install new subframe bolts and torque to specification.

title: Steering wheel shake only when braking from highway speed
text: Applies to all vehicles. A steering wheel shake that occurs only when braking from highway speed, and is absent when cruising, usually comes from front rotor thickness variation. Measure rotor runout and thickness variation with the wheels torqued to specification. Repair: replace or refinish the front rotors.

title: Warm air from passenger side only on dual-zone systems
text: Applies to all models with dual-zone automatic climate control. The driver side may blow cold while the passenger side blows warm because the passenger temperature door loses calibration. Run the climate control self-test and read stored HVAC codes. Repair: recalibrate the passenger temperature door actuator.

title: Warm AC after restart from electric compressor inverter
text: Applies to small crossovers with an electric AC compressor, model years 2022-2024. The AC may blow warm for several minutes after a restart because the compressor inverter is slow to initialize. Read compressor inverter codes with a scan tool, and note the time from restart until the vents cool. Keep the scan tool connected through several restarts to catch the code. Repair: update the compressor inverter software.

title: Harsh 1-2 upshift on a cold transmission
text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission. A harsh 1-2 upshift may occur only during the first few minutes of driving below 40 deg F and stop once the transmission warms. Review the transmission fluid temperature reading during the event. Let the vehicle cold-soak overnight so the event can be reproduced on the first drive. Repair: update the transmission control software.

title: Harsh 2-3 upshift after a battery disconnect
text: Applies to full-size pickups with the 5.5L V8, model years 2021-2023. A harsh 2-3 upshift may occur after a battery disconnect because shift adaptive values were cleared. Confirm the battery was recently disconnected, and run the shift adapt relearn drive cycle. The drive cycle needs a warm transmission and several light-throttle upshifts. Repair: reset the adaptive values and complete the relearn.

title: Lean codes at idle from a contaminated airflow sensor
text: Applies to gasoline engines with a mass airflow sensor, model years 2009-2022. Lean codes with high long-term fuel trim at idle may set when a contaminated sensor element under-reports airflow. With the engine warm and idling and all accessories off, read MAF airflow on a scan tool. Expect roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement. Do not touch the sensor element. Repair: clean the sensor element or replace the sensor.
step: With the engine warm and idling and the accessories off, read mass airflow on a scan tool and compare it with roughly 1 g/s per liter of displacement
results: The scan tool shows the MAF right about where it should be for my engine size at idle.
MAF reading at warm idle matched the 1 g/s per liter rule almost exactly.

title: Long crank on hot restarts from fuel pressure bleed-down
text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Rail pressure that bleeds down lets fuel boil in a hot rail and lengthens hot restarts. Drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later. It should stay above 30 psi. Repair: replace the leaking injector or the pump module.
step: Drive until the engine is fully warm, shut it off with a gauge on the fuel rail test port and read the pressure 20 minutes later; it should still be above 30 psi
results: Put a gauge on after a drive. Still 42 psi after twenty minutes.
Residual pressure held at about 40 psi twenty minutes after shutdown.

title: Long crank on hot restarts from overfueling
text: Applies to all gasoline engines. Overfueling can cause a long crank on hot restarts. On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator pedal held to the floor; the control module cuts injector pulse in this clear-flood mode. A noticeably faster start in clear-flood mode means the engine is being overfueled. Repair: correct the source, such as a leaking injector or a skewed temperature input.
step: On a hot restart, crank with the accelerator held to the floor to put the engine in clear-flood mode and note whether it fires noticeably faster
results: Tried it with the pedal floored on a hot restart. Cranked just as long, no difference.
The clear-flood trick made no difference. Still a long crank when it's hot.

title: Misfire under load from a tracked or fouled spark plug
text: Applies to all gasoline engines, model years 2010-2022. A single-cylinder misfire under load may come from a spark plug with a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or an excessive gap. Remove the plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a cylinder that is not misfiring. Check the gap against the underhood emissions label (typically 0.040-0.044 in). Repair: replace the spark plugs as a set.
step: Pull the spark plug from the misfiring cylinder and compare it with one from a good cylinder, checking the gap and looking for a cracked insulator, carbon tracking or fouling
results: Pulled the plug. Gap is 0.042, no cracks, and it looks like the others.
The plug from that cylinder looks clean and is gapped right, no tracking on the porcelain.

title: Overheating in traffic from an inoperative electric radiator fan
text: Applies to 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4, 2.5L I4, 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 1.4L turbo I4, 3.5L V6 and 3.4L V6 engines with electric radiator fans. Temperature may climb at idle and in traffic, but not at speed, if the fan does not run. With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the fan on with a scan tool. The fan should start within a few moments. Repair: repair the fan circuit or replace the fan motor.
step: With the engine warm and idling, turn the AC on or command the radiator fan on with a scan tool and confirm the fan starts
results: Turned the AC on and the radiator fan kicked on right away.
Commanded the fan with my scanner and it spun up on both speeds.

title: Overheating at idle from a restricted radiator core
text: Applies to all engines. Scale or debris in the radiator core can make temperature climb at idle and in traffic. With the engine warm and the thermostat open, compare the radiator inlet tank with the outlet tank using an infrared thermometer. A drop of 20-40 deg F is typical; a much smaller drop, or cold spots across the core, indicates restricted flow. Repair: flush or replace the radiator.
step: With the engine at operating temperature, compare the radiator inlet and outlet tank temperatures with an infrared thermometer and scan the core for cold spots
results: Inlet was 205 and outlet 172, and I didn't find any cold spots on the core.
About a 30 degree drop across the radiator and an even temperature across the core.

title: Coolant loss with no visible leak from an early-venting cap
text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans, small crossovers and compact crossovers, model years 2010-2021. Coolant may drop slowly with no visible leak when the pressure cap vents early and coolant escapes through the overflow as vapor. Fit the cap to a pressure tester adapter and pump until it vents. It should hold at least its stamped rating. Repair: replace the pressure cap.
step: Test the radiator or reservoir cap on a cap adapter and confirm it holds at least its stamped pressure rating
results: The cap held its rated 16 psi on the adapter.
Tested the cap and it didn't vent until past its rating.

title: Weak heat in cold weather from a thermostat stuck open
text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4 and 2.4L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Heater output may be weak in cold weather, with a low temperature gauge, when the thermostat sticks partly open. From a cold start, idle the engine and watch coolant temperature on a scan tool while feeling the upper radiator hose. It should stay cool until about 195 deg F. Repair: replace the thermostat and gasket.
step: From a cold start, watch coolant temperature on a scan tool while feeling the upper radiator hose; it should stay cool until about 195 deg F
results: The upper hose stayed cool until the scanner showed about 196, and it got hot fast after that.
Reached 195 in about eight minutes and the upper hose warmed right at that point.

title: Cool vent air from a skipping blend door actuator
text: Applies to all models. Vent air may stay cool, with a clicking noise behind the dash, when the blend door actuator skips or stops short of full hot. With the engine warm, run the climate control from full cold to full hot while listening behind the center of the dash. The actuator should move smoothly through its full travel. Repair: replace and recalibrate the blend door actuator.
step: With the engine warm, sweep the temperature control from full cold to full hot and listen behind the center of the dash for the blend door actuator moving through its full travel
results: I can hear the door move all the way across and it doesn't click or stop.
The actuator sweeps smoothly from cold to hot, no clicking.

title: Dead battery after parking from a circuit that stays awake
text: Applies to all vehicles, model years 2008-2021. A module or circuit that does not go to sleep can flatten the battery after several days parked. Latch the hood switch, close the doors and allow up to 45 minutes for the modules to sleep. Measure draw with an ammeter in series at the negative terminal. It should settle below 50 mA. Repair: isolate and correct the circuit that stays awake.
step: With the doors closed and the modules asleep, connect an ammeter in series at the negative battery terminal; draw should settle below 50 mA
results: Waited 45 minutes and the draw settled at 28 mA.
Meter read 0.03 amps once everything went to sleep.

title: Dim lights at idle from a slipping accessory belt
text: Applies to 1.6L I4, 1.8L I4, 2.0L I4, 2.4L I4 and 2.5L I4 engines, model years 2010-2020. Lights may dim at idle under load when a glazed belt or weak tensioner lets the alternator pulley slip. With the engine off, inspect the drive belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs, and confirm the tensioner indicator sits within its marked range. Repair: replace the belt and tensioner.
step: With the engine off, inspect the accessory belt for glazing, cracks and missing ribs and confirm the tensioner indicator is within its marked range
results: The belt looks new, no glazing, and the tensioner mark is in the middle of the range.
Belt and tensioner both look fine, no cracks.

title: Flickering lights from a failed alternator diode
text: Applies to all vehicles. Headlights may flicker or dim at idle because a failed rectifier diode reduces alternator output. With the engine running at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, set a meter to AC volts and measure across the battery posts. Ripple should be below 0.5 V AC. Repair: replace the alternator.
step: With the engine at about 1,500 rpm and the headlights on, measure AC ripple voltage across the battery posts and compare it with 0.5 V AC
results: Ripple was 0.08 volts AC.
AC ripple measured well under half a volt.

title: Click with no crank from the starter control circuit
text: Applies to vehicles with an automatic transmission or CVT, model years 2010-2021. The starter may click or stay silent in park when the range switch, starter relay or wiring drops voltage to the solenoid. Back-probe the solenoid S terminal and have a helper attempt a start in park. The S terminal should see at least 10.5 V during the attempt. Use a back-probe pin so the connector seal is not damaged. Repair: correct the switch, relay or wiring fault.
step: Back-probe the starter solenoid S terminal while a helper attempts a start in park; it should get at least 10.5 V
results: Got 11.8 volts at the S terminal when it clicks.
The S terminal sees about 11.5 V on the start attempt.

title: Brake pulsation from excessive rotor lateral runout
text: Applies to vehicles with front disc brakes. Pulsation may develop several thousand miles after a brake or wheel service when rotor lateral runout is high. With the lug nuts torqued to specification, mount a dial indicator to the knuckle with the plunger about 0.5 in from the rotor's outer edge and rotate the rotor one full turn. Runout must not exceed 0.002 in. Clean the hub face first. Repair: index the rotor on the hub or refinish it.
step: With the lug nuts torqued to spec, mount a dial indicator on the knuckle and measure front rotor lateral runout about half an inch in from the edge against the 0.002 in limit
results: Runout on both front rotors was 0.001 inch.
Dial indicator showed under a thousandth on both sides.

title: Pull during braking from binding caliper slide pins
text: Applies to vehicles with floating front calipers. A pull during braking may come from a corroded or swollen slide pin that binds and causes uneven pad pressure. Remove each front caliper from its bracket without disconnecting the hose, pull each slide pin and check for corrosion, a swollen boot or binding. Pins should move freely by hand. Repair: clean and lubricate the pins, or fit new pins and boots.
step: Remove the front calipers from their brackets and confirm each slide pin moves freely through its full travel without binding
results: Slide pins on both sides slide freely, no rust.
Pulled the pins on both calipers. Clean and they move fine.

title: Brake pull from a restricted front brake hose
text: Applies to midsize sedans and compact crossovers, model years 2011-2020. A pull during braking, sometimes with one front wheel running hot, may come from a front brake hose that collapses internally and restricts fluid return. With the front wheels raised, have a helper press and release the pedal firmly. Spin each front wheel by hand right after release; both should turn freely. Repair: replace both front brake hoses.
step: With the front wheels raised, have a helper press and release the brake pedal and spin each front wheel right away to see whether either one stays dragged
results: Both front wheels spin freely right after the pedal is released.
Neither wheel drags after letting off the pedal.

title: Front clunk over bumps from worn strut upper mounts
text: Applies to vehicles with front struts, model years 2010-2022. A worn strut upper mount or bearing can clunk over bumps or when turning slowly. With a helper bouncing the front, rest a hand on the upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock. With the engine running, turn lock to lock and feel for binding or a pop. Repair: replace the upper mounts and bearings.
step: With a helper bouncing the front of the vehicle, rest a hand on each strut upper mount under the hood and feel for a knock
results: Couldn't feel any knock at the top mounts while it was bounced.
Strut mounts feel quiet and solid when bouncing the front.

title: Steering wheel shake at highway speed from wheel imbalance
text: Applies to all vehicles. A steering wheel shake that peaks in a narrow band such as 60-70 mph may come from tire and wheel assemblies that are out of balance or have high road-force variation. Check each assembly on a road-force balancer. Imbalance should be under 0.25 oz and road-force variation under about 20 lb. Repair: rebalance the assemblies and match-mount as needed.
step: Check each wheel and tire on a road-force balancer for imbalance and road-force variation
results: A shop road-force balanced all four and they were all within spec.
Balance was fine on every wheel and the road-force numbers were low.

title: Pedal that sinks at a stop from master cylinder bypass
text: Applies to compact sedans, midsize sedans and hatchbacks, model years 2010-2020. Fluid bypassing the master cylinder seals lets the pedal sink slowly at a stop with no external leak. With the engine off, pump the pedal several times to use up booster reserve. Apply steady, moderate pressure and hold it for one minute. Watch the pedal height against a fixed mark. Repair: replace the master cylinder and bleed the system.
step: With the engine off and the booster reserve pumped out, hold steady moderate pressure on the pedal for one minute and watch whether it slowly sinks
results: Held it for a full minute with the engine off and the pedal didn't sink.
Pedal stayed put under steady pressure for the whole minute.

title: Warm AC at idle from an inoperative condenser fan
text: Applies to models with an electric condenser fan, model years 2009-2021. Vent air may warm up at idle and in traffic and cool again at speed when the condenser fan does not run. With the engine idling and the AC switched on, confirm the condenser fan runs. Without airflow across the condenser at idle, high-side pressure rises. Repair: correct the fan circuit fault or replace the fan motor.
step: With the engine idling and the AC on, confirm the condenser fan is running
results: The condenser fan comes on as soon as the AC is on.
Fan runs the whole time the AC is on.

title: Harsh engagement from high line pressure
text: Applies to vehicles with a conventional automatic transmission (not CVT or manual). A pressure control solenoid that holds line pressure high causes harsh engagements and firm shifts. Connect a gauge to the line pressure test port. Idling in drive with the brake applied, pressure should be 55-75 psi and rise with throttle. Repair: replace the pressure control solenoid.
step: Connect a gauge to the line pressure port and read line pressure at idle in drive with the brake applied; it should be 55-75 psi
results: Line pressure was 62 at idle in drive and rose normally.
Gauge read about 65 psi at idle in gear.
